title: Read replica lag
summary: A reporting query on T4's read replica (ContosoCare.Demo/replica-lag/<run>) reads demo.replica_lag_marks and holds its lock for holdSeconds, while T4 takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on that table once, in a short transaction, and keeps committing small marks. Replaying that lock on the replica waits for the report, up to max_standby_streaming_delay, so Read Replica Lag climbs to about holdSeconds, then drops when the report ends. It repeats in cycles until the run ends. PostgreSQL (T4) with its read replica only.

concurrency.description: Fixed: one report on the replica and one writer on T4 each cycle.

intensity.description: Not used: holdSeconds and markIntervalMs set the scenario's pace.

notes.T4: Needs T4's read replica, pgreplica01-<deploymentId>, which start-demo.ps1 creates for each session and whose name deploy.ps1 sends T1 (ADR 0025); without it the run is refused with that fix. The replica's max_standby_streaming_delay is 10 minutes, above holdSeconds' maximum, so each report ends by itself.

holdSeconds.description: How long each cycle's report on the replica holds demo.replica_lag_marks, so about how high the replica's lag climbs (a cycle is cut to end before the run's deadline).

pauseSeconds.description: Quiet time between cycles, after the lag has dropped.

markIntervalMs.description: How often the writer on T4 commits a small mark, while a report holds the table and for 30 seconds after it ends.

expectedHubSignals.signal: T4 replica: Read replica lag (physical_replication_delay_in_seconds) climbs to about holdSeconds, then drops
expectedHubSignals.note: On the replica's own PostgreSQL dashboard: Estate lists it as a server of its own (ADR 0025).

expectedHubSignals.signal: T4: Max Physical Replication Lag (physical_replication_delay_in_bytes) grows on the primary
expectedHubSignals.note: T4's metrics in the Azure portal; the replica's Read Replica Lag is there too.

expectedSymptoms: The replica stops replaying while the report runs: the time since its last replayed transaction grows by a second every second
The replica's startup process waits on a relation lock (Lock:relation) that the ContosoCare.Demo/replica-lag report holds
T4 keeps committing marks, so the WAL the replica has received but not replayed grows
When the report ends, or recovery cancels it at max_standby_streaming_delay (SQLSTATE 40001), replay catches up within seconds and the lag drops
queryLevelEvidence: ContosoCare.Workload status --target T4 --replica-server <fqdn>: the replica's replay lag and its demo sessions
On the replica: pg_stat_activity shows the report active (wait event PgSleep) and the startup process waiting on Lock:relation; pg_locks shows the report's AccessShareLock on demo.replica_lag_marks
On T4: pg_stat_replication's replay_lag grows, and replay_lsn stays behind sent_lsn
demo.scenario_run_events records replica-lag-locked, replica-report-ended (or replica-report-recovery-cancel), and replica-lag-recovered for each cycle
reset: Each report ends by itself, or by its statement_timeout before the run's deadline; the auto-cleanup and reset delete the marks, the only rows it writes. reset and stop with --replica-server also end the demo's sessions on the replica (pg_cancel_backend, then pg_terminate_backend).
